rows.title: AI
rows.contest: Whether the companies building AI should answer for the harm it causes, or whether its benefits justify letting society absorb some of that harm.
rows.stakes: Whether, when and by whom this new technology should be regulated, and who should share in its benefits, is still being settled. So is how to compete with China on it while still cooperating where both countries need to.

beginnings.line: Congress passed a law setting the terms of American relations with Taiwan, including the sale of defensive arms to the island.
Congress rewrote the nation's communications law in 1996, covering telephone, cable and broadcast, and for the first time the internet.
President Clinton signed a law giving China permanent normal trade status, ending the yearly congressional review of it.
Congress passed the USA PATRIOT Act soon after the terrorist attacks of that year, widening the government's powers to investigate and watch people.
China's National People's Congress adopted the Anti-Secession Law on 14 March 2005, a law about Taiwan.

objects.title: Taiwan Relations Act
objects.author: U.S. Congress
objects.about: The Taiwan Relations Act is a law passed by the U.S. Congress and signed on April 10, 1979. It lets the United States keep commercial and cultural ties with the people on Taiwan after formal relations ended. It says the U.S. expects Taiwan's future to be settled peacefully, and that it will provide Taiwan with defensive arms.

objects.title: Telecommunications Act of 1996
objects.author: U.S. Congress
objects.about: The Telecommunications Act of 1996 is a federal law passed by the U.S. Congress and signed by President Clinton on February 8, 1996. It rewrote federal rules for telephone, cable, and broadcast companies, including limits on how many stations one company could own.

objects.title: Permanent Normal Trade Relations with China, signing remarks
objects.author: William J. Clinton
objects.about: President Clinton gave these remarks on 10 October 2000 as he signed a law granting China permanent normal trade relations. The law ended the yearly congressional vote on China's trade status. The remarks are collected in the Public Papers of the Presidents.

objects.title: USA PATRIOT Act
objects.author: U.S. Congress
objects.about: Congress passed this law, Public Law 107-56, and the president signed it on 26 October 2001, soon after the terrorist attacks of that year. It widened the government's powers to investigate terrorism and to collect information, including electronic communications.

objects.title: Anti-Secession Law
objects.author: National People’s Congress of the PRC
objects.about: The Anti-Secession Law was passed by China's National People's Congress on 14 March 2005. It is a Chinese law about Taiwan. Its text is published by the National People's Congress.
